trials.name: Bapineuzumab 302 (ApoE4 Carrier)
trials.sponsor: JANSSEN Alzheimer Immunotherapy Research & Development, LLC
trials.population: Patients aged 50-88 with probable Alzheimer's disease, MMSE 16-26
trials.results_summary: Bapineuzumab did not significantly improve clinical outcomes (ADAS-cog11, DAD) compared to placebo. It reduced CSF phospho-tau and stabilized brain amyloid, but caused dose-dependent amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA-E).

trials.name: Bapineuzumab 301 (ApoE4 Non-Carrier)
trials.sponsor: JANSSEN Alzheimer Immunotherapy Research & Development, LLC
trials.population: Patients aged 50-88 with probable Alzheimer's disease, MMSE 16-26
trials.results_summary: Bapineuzumab failed to show significant differences compared to placebo on the primary endpoints. The study subsequently revealed that 36.1% of enrolled noncarriers were amyloid negative at baseline.

trials.name: Bapineuzumab 3001 (Global ApoE4 Carrier)
trials.population: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (ApoE4 carriers)
trials.results_summary: Trial was terminated in August 2012 due to the lack of clinical benefit observed in the North American Phase 3 trials. Peer-reviewed results confirmed the lack of efficacy on primary endpoints.

trials.name: Bapineuzumab 3000 (Global ApoE4 Non-Carrier)
trials.population: Mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (ApoE4 non-carriers)
trials.results_summary: Terminated in August 2012 alongside NCT00676143 due to failure of the North American trials. Did not show clinical benefit in preserving cognitive or functional performance.

trials.name: Bapineuzumab 201 (Multiple Ascending Dose)
trials.sponsor: JANSSEN Alzheimer Immunotherapy Research & Development, LLC
trials.results_summary: No significant differences were found on primary efficacy analysis, though exploratory analyses hinted at benefit in APOE ε4 noncarriers, leading to the bifurcated Phase 3 design. Characterized vasogenic edema (ARIA-E) risks.

related_evidence.description: Primary publication of the North American Phase 3 bapineuzumab trials showing lack of clinical efficacy (Salloway et al., NEJM).
Phase 2 multiple ascending dose trial results detailing vasogenic edema side effects and a lack of primary clinical benefit (Salloway et al., Neurology).
Results from the terminated global Phase 3 trials confirming lack of clinical efficacy for bapineuzumab (Vandenberghe et al., Alzheimers Res Ther).

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence robustly and unequivocally demonstrates that bapineuzumab fails to provide clinical benefit for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. The drug's failure was verified across four large, independent Phase 3 trials (two in North America and two globally) that separated patients by APOE ε4 carrier status. While biomarker data in carriers confirmed central target engagement—including reduced CSF phospho-tau and stabilized brain amyloid—these pharmacodynamic effects did not translate into cognitive or functional improvements on the ADAS-cog11 or DAD scales. Due to this consistent lack of efficacy and dose-limiting safety concerns, most notably a high incidence of ARIA-E, the entire intravenous bapineuzumab development program was terminated in 2012.
